{"markdown": "The subject of this report is the credit_default model package, a binary classifier whose output is the probability that a borrower defaults, and the report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management guidance, under which outcomes analysis compares model outputs to the corresponding real-world outcomes and is reviewed for reasonableness against established performance thresholds [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.b]].
The validation ran the packaged subject end to end and recomputed each reported metric from the subject's own predictions, within the wall-clock cap of 300.0 seconds [[art:3f4c6e97:threshold.package.max_seconds]] that package.yaml declares.
The train split holds 21000 rows [[art:a359de9d:profile.train.n]] and the test split holds 9000 rows [[art:abbe1a27:profile.test.n]], and recomputation covered 21000 rows [[art:1721ceae:metrics.train.n]] on train and 9000 rows [[art:5367a59f:metrics.test.n]] on test.

On the test split the model stays inside every threshold the developer declared.
The area under the ROC curve is 0.755 [[art:365b7034:metrics.test.auc]], above the declared minimum of 0.7 [[art:8bfd02cc:threshold.package.auc.test.min]].
The Brier score is 0.1385 [[art:86e93c8f:metrics.test.brier]], below the declared maximum of 0.2 [[art:d0f98b9c:threshold.package.brier.test.max]].
The calibration slope is 0.9886 [[art:e06564c7:calibration_slope.test]], inside the declared band running from 0.8 [[art:95fdb848:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.min]] to 1.2 [[art:0adb7a89:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.max]].
The largest train-to-test population stability index, score included, is 0.003083 [[art:e1d82330:psi.max]], below the declared maximum of 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]].

Further diagnostics carry no declared bound and are reported for context rather than judged against one.
The largest characteristic stability index is 0.004737 [[art:ce1257d8:csi.max]], the largest variance inflation factor is 3.544 [[art:d3785ba9:vif.max]], and Belsley's condition number of the column-standardised design is 4.279 [[art:ba0d9cc4:condition_number]].

No findings were raised at any severity: every check that ran on this section's material returned nothing to report."}

1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 1. Summary and scope

What this section must do:
Open with one sentence that says what the model is, what it predicts, and which guidance this
report follows, anchored by a [[reg:...]] citation. Then state how the subject was run and how
large each split is, then the headline result: which developer-declared thresholds the model
passes, each with the value and the bound, and how many findings were raised at which severity.
Do not describe a check that has no artifact in the JSON below.

Rules, all of them checked after you answer:
- Every number you write is followed immediately by its [[art:...]] citation, copied exactly from
  the JSON below. A number with no citation is counted against this report.
- Write no number that is not in the JSON below. If you want to say something the artifacts do not
  support, say it in words without a number.
- One sentence per line. The claim extractor works line by line, so a sentence split over two
  lines is two claims and a paragraph on one line is one.
- For a table artifact, do not retype the cells. Write the directive [[table:<logical_name>]] on a
  line of its own; the renderer expands it, with its caption and its citation, from the store.
- Open the section with a sentence that anchors it to the guidance, carrying one [[reg:...]]

- Do not use the words "compliant" or "certified".

  "text": "Outcomes analysis compares model outputs to corresponding real-world outcomes to\nassess model performance relative to model objectives and business use. In such cases, model\nadjustment, recalibration, or redevelopment may be warranted.\nOutcomes analysis can take many forms, including testing conducted during model\ndevelopment, reports or analysis performed as part of ongoing monitoring, or standalone\nactivities such as back-testing or outlier analysis. A banking organization\u2019s approach depends on\nthe model\u2019s objectives, methodology, and data availability. As part of model validation, sound\npractice involves reviewing outcomes analysis to evaluate the reasonableness and\nappropriateness of the results, with additional analysis and testing, if warranted. When a model\u2019s\ndesign relies substantially on expert judgment, quantitative outcomes analysis helps to evaluate\nthe quality of that judgment."
 },

  "heading": "Purpose and Scope",
  "text": "The purpose of this document is to provide comprehensive guidance for banks on\neffective model risk management. Rigorous model validation plays a critical role in\nmodel risk management; however, sound development, implementation, and use of\nmodels are also vital elements. Furthermore, model risk management encompasses\ngovernance and control mechanisms such as board and senior management oversight,\npolicies and procedures, controls and compliance, and an appropriate incentive and\norganizational structure.\nPrevious guidance and other publications issued by the OCC and the Federal Reserve on\nthe use of models pay particular attention to model validation. [Footnote 2\n- For instance, the OCC provided guidance on model risk, focusing on model validation, in OCC 2000-16\n(May 30, 2000), other bulletins, and certain subject matter booklets of the Comptroller's Handbook. The\nFederal Reserve issued SR Letter 09-01, \"Application of the Market Risk Rule in Bank Holding Companies\nand State Member Banks,\" which highlights various concepts pertinent to model risk management,\nincluding standards for validation and review, model validation documentation, and back-testing. The\nFederal Reserve's Trading and Capital-Markets Activities Manual also discusses validation and model risk\nmanagement. In addition, the advanced-approaches risk-based capital rules (12 CFR 3, Appendix C; 12\nCFR 208, Appendix F; and 12 CFR 225, Appendix G) contain explicit validation requirements for subject\nbanking organizations. End of Footnote 2.]\nBased on supervisory and\nindustry experience over the past several years, this document expands on existing\nguidance\u2014most importantly by broadening the scope to include all aspects of model risk\nmanagement.
